description: Reviewed Ultron A01-A46 acceptance instrument. Evidence tests are matched by name substring against vitest JSON results (fullName). Change only through a recorded review, then run npm run acceptance:lock.

rows.behavior: Direct/graph/RLM invocation shares one definition and result contract

tests: the same definition yields the same validated result and durable task record on all three paths
schema-invalid output fails identically on all three paths and is never recorded as success
invalid input is rejected before admission on all three paths with the same error

rows.notes: Direct, workflow-graph and Python-kernel invocation share one validated result and durable record; invalid input/output fails identically.

rows.behavior: Large input stays outside active context; full data remains usable

tests: the rlm tool computes exact aggregates over all rows while its result stays bounded
the request after the rlm call carries the aggregate, not the dataset

rows.notes: ~10 MB dataset stays in the kernel; rlm results are bounded (~24.6 KB) and an end-to-end model request carries only the computed answer.

rows.behavior: Invalid result triggers bounded repair or typed failure

tests: predict repairs a semantically invalid result within maxRepairs and reports the repair
predict stops after maxRepairs and fails typed without returning the malformed answer
maxRepairs 0 makes exactly one attempt, and more than 2 repairs cannot be registered
non-JSON and throwing predict adapters fail typed
rlm malformed JSON and schema-invalid output fail typed after one bounded attempt
one call per attempt, repair with the validation error, no lane or kernel
exhausted repairs fail typed instead of claiming success

rows.notes: Predict repairs within maxRepairs through the production predict adapter; rlm output never repairs and fails typed.

rows.behavior: Root pin and explicit child model are preserved

tests: an explicit child model reaches only the child lane; the root lane's model is never changed

rows.notes: Explicit child models reach only the child lane; the root lane model is never changed. Live model use is recorded by the A39 suite.

rows.behavior: Cancellation terminates owned work and rejects late success

tests: cancelling a running cell kills its whole process tree, including a setsid grandchild
shutdown also terminates the owned tree of a cell blocked in synchronous code
cancelling a native task aborts its lane, kills the lane kernel's process tree, and keeps the durable cancelled result
a delayed provider success after cancellation never overwrites the durable cancelled result
racing cancellation against provider success always yields one durable, consistent terminal result
runs an explicit background job through the same durable task host
runs deterministic agents and preserves durable task records
concurrent idempotent invokes share the same live promise
cancellation commits a terminal result without waiting for a stuck lane
parent cancellation before admission does not start a task
timeout has a bounded range and commits cancellation
reopened invoke returns the durable result, not undefined
only a completed prompt at its returned tip can succeed
validates every workflow node, normalizes missing dependencies, and skips failed dependencies
rejects malformed reviewer output instead of claiming success

rows.notes: Linux: cancellation kills the kernel's whole process tree, including setsid descendants; late success never overwrites a cancelled result.

rows.behavior: Output, artifact, wall-time, concurrency, and process limits hold

tests: stdout, stderr, and result previews stay bounded under a 50 MB flood
raw writes that bypass Python's stdout are cut off at the protocol frame limit
oversize artifacts and quota overflow are rejected without being stored
an artifact larger than the RPC frame never reaches the service from Python
a task past its timeout is cancelled with a durable cancelled result
the root wall deadline caps task timeouts and rejects work after it passes
an interrupted runaway cell stops, and the kernel serves the next cell
interrupting a cell kills its child and grandchild processes
shutting down the kernel kills the whole process tree

rows.notes: Trusted-local profile: output, artifact, wall-time, admission and process-group limits. No memory/CPU limits or isolated profile exist.

rows.behavior: Branch/fork/resume restores matching state; no abandoned lesson leak

tests: resume after restart restores tasks, definitions, lessons, progress, memory and usage from real session values
a fork starts from the source state, then lessons written on either side never leak to the other across restarts
rolling back a lesson on one branch before a restart does not resurrect it, and the other branch keeps its own
a lesson from an abandoned branch never applies after navigating away, and each branch keeps its own

rows.notes: Resume and fork restore matching state; refinements are anchored to the conversation branch, so a lesson from an abandoned branch never applies.

rows.behavior: Unsupported Python state reports non-restorable, never silently correct

tests: snapshot type matrix saves plain data and reports every unsupported name with a reason
restore brings back equal values of the same types and reports the non-restorable names as absent
startup restore from a configured snapshot reports the same non-restorable names
a tampered snapshot body is rejected and leaves the namespace untouched
snapshots without a valid header or with a forged digest over malformed data are rejected
a kernel configured with a tampered snapshot fails startup instead of starting with wrong state

rows.notes: Constrained tagged snapshot format with a sha256 header; unsupported names are reported, tampering is rejected. Integrity, not authenticity: a writer who recomputes the digest is not detected.

rows.behavior: Concurrent calls/retries cannot bypass tree budget admission

tests: a burst of concurrent spawns admits exactly the limit and rejects the rest
nested children spawned from child lanes share the root tree budget
idempotent retries neither consume a slot nor release the live original's slot
the root wall deadline caps child deadlines and refuses admission once spent
missing usage and unknown pricing stay unknown, never zero
direct ledger reservations race to exactly the limit
later tasks with the default timeout are capped to the remaining root budget, not refused

rows.notes: Task-count and wall-deadline admission cannot be bypassed by races, nesting or retries. No monetary cap exists to test.

rows.behavior: Worker receives no ambient credentials or unauthorized host capability

tests: model-written Python sees no ambient credentials or worker control channel
explicit allow-list passes a named variable through

rows.notes: Python kernels receive no credential-like variables or worker control channel; host capabilities exist only as host requests.

rows.behavior: Approval binds scope/revision/policy and is rechecked

tests: issues a grant owned by the calling lane and allows a matching check
revocation denies later checks, and only the owner lineage may revoke
expiry is rechecked against the clock on every check
a changed base, policy, scope, or action is denied
descendants of the owner may use a grant; siblings and the root may not
rejects a forged owner and other unknown or malformed fields
enforce defaults to false and is reported; opting in reports true
grants and revocations survive a new module instance
checkGrant is a pure evaluation that reports every failing binding

rows.notes: Grants bind scope, revision, policy, action, owner and expiry and are rechecked on every use. Dormant by default (enforce: false) per the no-friction amendment.

rows.behavior: Graph validates before effects; routes/skips/fan-in/cycles are explicit

tests: every validation error is raised before any task is admitted or any node runs
a node whose definition cannot execute is rejected before effects
fan-in receives every dependency's result, keyed by dependency ID
a failed dependency yields explicit, transitive skip records while independent siblings complete
conditional routes are explicit: the matching branch runs, the other is skipped with a reason
a bound input that fails the node's schema is an explicit failed node, with nothing spawned for it
refused admission is an explicit failed node and does not abort running siblings

rows.notes: Validation before effects, fan-in, conditional routes, explicit skips and failures. Any-of joins and bounded revision cycles are not implemented.

rows.behavior: Agent admission does not satisfy a graph dependency

tests: a dependent is not admitted or started until the slow dependency's result is durable
agents.spawn confirms admission only; the result is not available until the task ends
a dependency that ends unsuccessfully skips its dependent, and a late valid result cannot revive it

rows.behavior: No checks/incomplete review/stale receipt cannot imply verified completion

tests: every task result path is unverified, and a stored 'verified' result is refused
reviewer output missing required fields fails; an incomplete review verifies nothing
a progress completion claim is verified only by a host-run verifier that returns passed: true
a goal with no required checks, or a check without an explicit pass, is never achieved
a release gate blocks on a missing required check or a stale fixture
a receipt for a stale revision is denied

rows.behavior: Baseline versus candidate is recorded; required regressions block

tests: passes when every required check passes in the candidate
a required regression blocks
an optional regression is reported but does not block
a required check missing or failed in the candidate blocks even without a baseline pass
a gate definition is frozen once defined
a fixture mismatch blocks with a reason
every attempt, blocked or passed, is recorded in history
rejects unknown fields and unknown gates
gates and attempts survive a new module instance, and tampered definitions are refused

rows.notes: Frozen gate definitions are the protected checker input; required regressions block via gates.compare.

rows.behavior: Memory skip causes no retrieval; scopes survive consolidation

tests: a Jev skip decision sends no request of any kind to Hindsight, for every scope and entry point
scope tags are pinned through retain, correction and Hindsight consolidation; a cross-scope merge is refused
recall after a real consolidation returns only items carrying exactly the requested scope's tags

rows.notes: Skip and scope pinning against the Hindsight adapter by default; consolidation is proven by a recorded run against a live Hindsight 0.9.2 (ULTRON_LIVE_HINDSIGHT=1).

rows.behavior: Correction supersedes stale claims; hypotheses remain distinguishable

tests: a corrected Pi launcher path is current and the stale claim superseded in later fresh sessions
hypotheses, user statements, tool evidence and verified conclusions stay distinct and validated

rows.behavior: Ingestion acceptance is distinct from completed retention; forgetting persists

tests: accepted-but-pending stays distinct from stored through receipt, backend failure and restart
a crash during dispatch reopens as unknown with no replay
forget persists across restart and outranks a backend that still returns the item
a forget whose delete fails is unknown, not forgotten, and still withholds the item after restart

rows.notes: Backend restart is simulated with the fake Hindsight.

rows.behavior: Refiner cannot alter policy, grants, or acceptance tests

tests: proposals targeting policy, grants, acceptance tests, the instrument lock or trusted instructions are rejected
content that requests tools, grants, models, budgets or permissions is rejected at proposal and activation
escalation prose inside an allowed instruction is inert data: grants and other state are unchanged

rows.behavior: Versioned refinement changes later behavior and can roll back

tests: activation reaches later model runs, a new version supersedes it, and rollback removes it

rows.notes: Active instruction refinements reach later task prompts; a new version supersedes; rollback removes it.

rows.behavior: Replay does not duplicate external effects; uncertainty stays explicit

tests: a lost response followed by an owner crash is not replayed, and the same key returns the durable interrupted result
crashes before launch, after the effect's response, and after commit never duplicate the effect

rows.behavior: Detached work and retained children survive UI loss

tests: a background child keeps running after its client quits and a new client reattaches to it
detached work finishes with no client attached, retires, and stays durable for a later client
quitting with no active work leaves no processes behind

rows.notes: Linux: busy workers survive client exit and are reattached; idle exit cleans up. A hard-killed client leaves work to the 30 s orphan grace.

rows.behavior: Schedules/goals/verification compose within budgets

tests: duplicate and concurrent ticks in the same slot run the slot once
a restart on the same stores does not re-run a completed or claimed slot
missed ticks coalesce into one run for the latest slot and record the skipped count
max_runs completes a schedule and pause stops firings
a paused goal stops attached schedule firings and resume re-enables them
required gate: achieved only when every required check succeeds with passed === true
max_tasks caps schedule firings, verification, and attachments
admission failure from the usage budget is recorded once per slot without a retry storm
the background timer fires due slots and stops on close
rejects unknown payload fields and forged identity

rows.behavior: Costs, task transitions, and inspection agree on one record

tests: reconstructs a mixed run from the journal, ledger, progress and schedule records and matches agents.status
a crashed owner's open work reconciles as interrupted and unknown after restart, and tampering is detected

rows.behavior: Existing Pi capabilities and data survive migration and rollback

tests: imports the active branch with exact messages, compaction tail, skipped types, name, and tip
refuses to re-import the same Pi session
rejects files that are not Pi sessions
round-trips Pi -> native -> Pi with the same active-branch messages and context
backs up the profile privately with a manifest and excludes sessions
rehearses restore: every profile file comes back byte-identical and sessions are untouched
refuses a tampered backup without touching the profile
refuses backups with unlisted files or unsafe manifest paths
ignores non-migrate commands
prints usage and rejects bad arguments
runs import, export, backup, and restore end to end without printing secrets
reconstructs Pi turn and agent boundaries from lane events
runs prompts, bash, and session commands through the native worker

rows.notes: Pi session import/export round trip and profile backup/restore rehearsal. Only the active branch is imported; labels and model changes are reported as skipped.

rows.behavior: Component changes cannot pass merely by weakening tests
rows.notes: Evidence is the instrument lock plus the mutation slice (acceptance/mutation.json); a surviving mutation holds the row unverified. Independent human review of the instrument remains a process step.

rows.behavior: RLM handles a self-contained task without graph/delegation/memory/refinement

tests: a real kernel parses and aggregates data with zero host dispatches
the task completes when every optional service rejects, and a service call fails explicitly
the rlm tool over a native host without optional services completes with no dispatches and no tasks

rows.behavior: Retrieval explanation/query/scope match the executed search; rewrite cannot widen access

tests: the recorded decision equals the request the backend received
a gate that tries to rewrite the query or escalate scope cannot change the executed search
gate or rewrite failure reports memory unavailable without searching
an unauthorized scope is denied before the gate or backend, and the denial is recorded
a compatible repeat reuses the recorded decision; refresh, changed input and mutation re-query

rows.behavior: Memory inspector shows actual injected evidence without a new search or hidden-scope disclosure

tests: why shows the evidence that was injected, with no new search and no other task's scope
the inspector refuses requests that would search or change state

rows.behavior: Correction/deletion propagates to managed memory views/exports without changing trusted instructions

tests: forgotten and corrected memories leave every view; AGENTS.md is untouched
a lagging backend index cannot re-inject a forgotten memory
forgetting persists across a new service instance on the same store

rows.behavior: Skill selection is version-pinned, explainable, and cannot grant capabilities

tests: lists skills with content-hash versions and invocability
select explains each candidate, ranks deterministically, and records the decision
why returns the original decision after the catalog changes
version-pinned load succeeds and a stale version is rejected
capability-granting frontmatter is reported and never reaches the spawned child
invoke through the real host keeps the child's model and tools and links the parent
concurrent loads, selects, and invokes each observe one catalog snapshot while content changes
disableModelInvocation skills are listed but cannot be invoked
rejects unknown payload fields, forged identity, and malformed arguments
durable state survives a new module instance and records catalog changes across restarts

rows.behavior: Skill proposals require evidence, validation, and applicable approval; rejection/rollback holds

tests: a repeated-procedure proposal activates only with evidence and records that approval is disabled
an equivalent pending or active proposal is a duplicate; a real change is not
invalid skill content fails validation, and enabled approval cannot override it
rejection and rollback hold across restart; a declined proposal needs new evidence to resurface
the worker's refinement service refuses malformed skills and accepts a loadable SKILL.md

rows.notes: Approval is disabled by default and recorded as not_required.

rows.behavior: Experiment history includes all attempts and variants do not contaminate each other

tests: every attempt, including crashed, failed and incomplete ones, is recorded against the frozen fixture
variants with isolated memory and refinement state never see each other's writes
per-variant usage, including failed and incomplete attempts, reconciles with independent metering

rows.notes: Ledger and service level; variant isolation relies on callers giving each variant separate stores.

rows.behavior: Optional-service failure preserves RLM operation without bypassing required checks or replaying effects

tests: combined Jev, Hindsight, refinement, module, and workflow outage in one real RLM kernel run

rows.behavior: Deterministic/predict/rlm methods share policy, validation, accounting, and task semantics

tests: only rlm launches a lane; predict and deterministic never start an iterative kernel
the same validation and result contract applies to every strategy
idempotency keys behave identically across strategies
timeout and cancellation commit the same cancelled result and abort the work for every strategy
usage reservations and durable journal transitions match across strategies

rows.behavior: Invocation scratch is isolated while declared instance state persists

tests: continue on the same lane with fresh scratch, and never rewrite the earlier result
reject concurrent use, closed instances, non-parents, and laneless tasks
an instance survives an owner restart and keeps its lane
reset clears scratch and restores bindings while declared state persists

rows.behavior: Bounded preview preserves full values and does not execute unsafe introspection on the host

tests: large values get a bounded preview while the full value stays usable in later cells
cyclic and deeply nested objects render without infinite recursion
a raising __repr__ does not fail the cell and the value remains usable
a sleeping __repr__ cannot hang the protocol; the kernel stays usable
enormous repr/str output and protocol-looking text stay bounded and inert
hostile exception __str__ (huge, raising, sleeping) yields a bounded error report
range reads return exact byte ranges, including ranges that split multibyte characters

rows.notes: A hostile repr that swallows BaseException can stall a cell until host cancellation kills the kernel.

rows.behavior: Nested context excludes unauthorized and contaminating history

tests: reviewer and RLM child lanes receive only their own prompt, not root history
each lane gets its own Python kernel, so root variables do not leak into a child
a child lane sees its own subtree only; siblings are indistinguishable from missing

rows.notes: Child lanes start empty and can query only their own subtree.

rows.behavior: Configured models can use the actual typed RLM interface
rows.notes: Metered live suite (ULTRON_LIVE_EVAL=1). The default run skips it; the row passes only on recorded runs in which every case qualified.

rows.behavior: Retained instances accept new invocations without rewriting old terminal outcomes

tests: continue on the same lane with fresh scratch, and never rewrite the earlier result
reject concurrent use, closed instances, non-parents, and laneless tasks
an instance survives an owner restart and keeps its lane
reset clears scratch and restores bindings while declared state persists

rows.behavior: Family messages enforce identity, scope, deduplication, expiry, and safe delivery

tests: rejects forged sender fields and takes the sender from the calling lane
delivers between parent and child in both directions, including root
rejects siblings, grandchildren, and other families
replays a keyed send idempotently and rejects conflicting content under the same key
never delivers expired messages and reports them as expired
rejects sends to a full inbox and oversized messages instead of dropping
receive is at-most-once and respects limit and FIFO order
steers a live receiver through the host and falls back to the inbox otherwise
isolates verifiers to their direct parent and never steers them
validates payloads strictly
durable state survives a new module instance on the same store
serializes concurrent sends against the inbox cap
derives identity from real task lanes and steers a live child lane

rows.behavior: Human child intervention and subtree stop preserve unrelated work

tests: inspect, correct, and stop one child's subtree while the sibling continues and completes
stopping a finished child still stops its live descendants and leaves siblings alone

rows.behavior: Resource release/eviction respects live references, evidence retention, and quotas

tests: idle eviction skips a running cell and a pinned lane, and evicts idle unpinned kernels after the TTL
capacity evicts the least recently used idle kernel and otherwise fails with a typed result
snapshot-before-evict records non-restorable names and a recreated kernel restores the rest
a failed snapshot refuses eviction and keeps the live kernel and its state
a pinned checkpoint artifact survives delete and reclaim; unpinned artifacts are reclaimed explicitly
quota failures are explicit and never evict artifacts to make room
a second lane evicts the idle first one after a snapshot, and the first lane's state comes back

rows.behavior: Progress and reassessment use evidence and cannot extend budgets or declare unsupported success

tests: classifies stalled, progressing, busy, and finished from recorded evidence
takes the reporter from the lane and rejects reports for unrelated tasks
validates payloads strictly and bounds evidence and receipts
always denies budget extension and records the reason
never verifies a completion claim without a passing verifier
persists receipts and decisions across module instances and settles interrupted verifications
rejects a corrupt stored document

rows.behavior: Saturated nested recursion makes progress or returns bounded capacity failure, never deadlock

tests: a parent awaiting children at saturation gets bounded capacity failures and still completes
cancelling a saturated parent cancels its waiting children and releases every slot

rows.behavior: The combined system performs the full demonstration without manual state repair

tests: fix, review, retain, and improve with real runtime effects
failure variants never become verified completion
fixes, reviews, retains, and improves through the typed RLM API

rows.notes: Deterministic demonstration and failure variants run by default; the live-model demonstration (ULTRON_LIVE_EVAL=1) must have a recorded passing run.
